_blind_means: Given the pinned sha and the outgoing artifact set and nothing else. Forbidden research/autonomy/ (every other seat record, the hardening state, the receipts, the ledger, the sprint notes, round33-seats and round34-prepin-seat), .claude/, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, STRATEGY.md, every *-cover-letter.md, every fusion-junction-aso-paper-redteam*.md and the guard-coverage audit. Told that blindness is a property of its commands rather than its intentions, given the scoped git grep form, and told to DISCLOSE any leak rather than discard the finding. Instructed to refute by default, told never to write an identifier from recollection or grade a PMID from memory, and told in words that returning no findings is a complete and expected answer.
lens: Traced every identifier the outgoing set prints back to a committed fetch record or ledger entry, then asked of each whether it is the identifier for the claim it is attached to. Parsed all 24 journal reference entries and compared title, year, volume, pages and DOI field-by-field against the deposited Europe PMC/PubMed records; read the deposited verbatim behind the load-bearing citations (the five-step industry framework, the RNase-H gap-length range, the FISH 'irrespective of partner' clause, the pazopanib response categories, the USZ cell-model junction annotations, the RRIDs) rather than grading from memory. Recomputed every printed count reachable from the released artifacts (87/61/85 liable, 45.8% vs 40.6%, 10.0%/3.9% scramble null, 176 distinct sequences with 9 at more than one exon pair, 68.4%/79.0% coverage, dTm 26.6/36.0). Hashed every one of the 516 manifest paths at the pin against the manifest's recorded digests, hashed all seven build-stamp inputs, extracted text from the four PDFs and three .docx files and checked their reference numbering, in-body citation markers and Data-availability wording against the markdown. Finally diffed the tree at the pin against 4fd4698daec0 — the revision the published Zenodo record 22229096 was built from — path by path against the manifest's own inventory, and read the deposited copies of the files that differ.
what_i_read: the four article PDFs and the three .docx files, with their seven build stamps
central_claim: Two named 16-mer 5-6-5 gapmers — 5'-GGGCATATCATCAAAC-3' at EWSR1 exon 12 and 5'-GGGCATATCTTGTGTG-3' at TAF15 exon 6, both to NR4A3 exon 3 — are synthesis-ready research reagents against the two most-reported EMC fusion junctions, each holding the panel's top gap-level margin of three and neither pairing a mature wild-type parent through its whole catalytic gap at the adopted ten-base-pair criterion (longest eight and nine bp, both against wild-type TFG). The paper's central negative is that this parent liability is not resolved: 87 of 190 junction-spanning designs (45.8%) let a wild-type parent pair their entire gap, chimeras built at real exon termini meet the same screen at 40.6% — inside the panel's own 95% interval at every cut from seven to thirteen but eleven — so most of the liability is what joining two exon termini of these genes gives, and no cut in the range is a boundary the data picks out. Selection within each junction rather than across the panel is what makes the two reagents available at all, and the ten-base-pair cut is adopted rather than measured. Everything is hybridisation prediction, not cleavage: no sequence has been synthesised or tested, and the paper names a pre-registrable isogenic knockdown experiment with two screened scramble controls as the test that would falsify the ranking.
_blockers_empty_means: Every identifier in the four outgoing markdown artifacts resolves to a committed fetch record with matching bibliographic fields; the built renderings are byte-current with the markdown they cite; and the archive the paper's DOI resolves to contains every file the paper's Data availability promises, with the manifest's own gaps.promises_resolving_to_no_file and promises_whose_sentence_is_no_longer_in_the_manuscript both empty at the pin. The seat looked hard at the deposit drift recorded below and could not make it a blocker: not one number the outgoing journal article prints moves between the deposited revision and the pin.

p1s.summary: The outgoing reference list's year, title, volume, pages and DOI are hand-typed and bound to no fetch record — only the author segment, the journal name and the PMID-to-superscript pairing are guarded. The entries are all correct today (all 24 checked field-by-field against the deposited records), but an ordinary edit — retyping a year, adding an entry, fixing a page range — would silently break one and nothing would go red. The sibling manuscript has exactly this guard and this one does not, so the pair is inverted.
p1s.evidence: fusion-junction-aso-journal-references.md lines 34-36 say so in its own banner. test_journal_references_match_the_prose.py opens only the article and the references file (lines 37-38) plus aso/journal-reference-authors.json for the author segment (line 148); test_each_entry_carries_the_pmid_its_citation_names compares the entry's 'PMID: N' against the article's own <!--PMID:N--> comment, both sides typed in this repository. lint_citations.py anchors an identifier only by requiring the string to appear in some tracked .json, so swapping a real DOI for a different real tracked DOI would pass. The counterpart guard is research/manuscripts/tests/test_the_endpoint_reference_list_binds_to_what_was_fetched.py.

p2s.summary: The published archive is 25 deposited paths behind the pin (24 changed, 1 added). The outgoing article, tables and references are byte-identical between the deposit revision and the pin, so the archive carries the same paper that cites it and no printed number moves; none of the 24 changed paths is a screen artifact or a number source for this article. Worth recording: the declaration of the drift lives in the preprint checklist, which is not deposited and is not an outgoing artifact, so a reader following the DOI gets no statement that the archive is behind.
